claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 18 and he's still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful context.

Since Alex is 18 and in approved education (A-levels), he could potentially qualify for Child Benefit. However, I need to understand your living situation better.

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. That's an important detail.

Now I need to ask about your residency status in the UK:

**Are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme? If neither, do you have any other right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that you're in Manchester. However, I need a bit more specific information about your residency status:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have any other immigration status such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another visa that gives you the right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you mean - yes, I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Now I have one more important question to help complete the picture:

**Is Alex still in full-time education at college, or does he also work? If he does work, is it 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work - he's just focused on his studies at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to make a determination.

Let me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Excellent news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex is under 20 and in approved education**: At 18 years old and studying A-levels at college, Alex qualifies for Child Benefit as he's in approved education or training.
- **You live with Alex**: This establishes that you are responsible for him.
- **You're a British citizen living in the UK**: You have the right to reside in the UK.
- **Alex is not working full-time**: Since he doesn't work 24 hours or more per week, there's no bar to eligibility.

You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex. If you'd like to proceed with a claim, you can do so through the official government website or contact HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) for guidance on how to apply.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
